warnings: no_customer_corpus: no interviews, win/loss, on-site search or authorised conversation data was supplied; every ICP is a public-evidence hypothesis
one_first_party_behavioural_source: only source-006 is direct buyer-written language; review-platform and community sources were blocked at access time
no_human_approval: Gate 1 is pending; no ICP has been promoted by a human

icps.label: Short-trip leisure traveller to a single foreign destination who wants working phone data on arrival without home-carrier roaming charges

context.geography: outbound from any market to a single declared destination

triggers.text: Upcoming trip abroad and awareness that home-carrier roaming is charged per day
Community threads asking which data option to buy for a named destination before flying

roles.label: traveller who installs and uses the line

constraints.text: Device must support eSIM and be network unlocked
Installation requires an existing internet connection
Plan is bound to one destination or destination set

disqualifiers.text: Carrier-locked handset; reported as the most common new-user failure
Handsets sold in China, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan may lack eSIM support

open_questions: What share of buyers purchase pre-departure versus after landing? No first-party data available.
Which destinations dominate demand? Only Japan, Bali, New Zealand and Europe appear in the retrieved community evidence.

icps.label: Multi-country traveller who needs one data plan that survives border crossings across a region or several continents

context.unit: individual traveller or couple on a multi-stop itinerary
context.itinerary_shape: several countries within one region, or a multi-region trip
context.geography: regional (for example multi-country Europe or Asia) and global

triggers.text: Itinerary crosses borders, making per-country purchases repetitive
Multi-host-country event travel concentrates demand for cross-border data

roles.label: traveller managing connectivity across the itinerary
trip organiser advising fellow travellers in forums

constraints.text: Regional and global packages cover defined country lists, not everywhere
Global plans are described as covering 137 countries; coverage lists must be checked per plan

disqualifiers.text: Traveller staying in a single country where a local plan is cheaper

open_questions: No independent buyer-language evidence was retrieved that is specific to multi-continent global plans as distinct from regional plans.

icps.label: Heavy-data traveller or remote worker who tethers a laptop and is exposed to fair-use throttling on unlimited plans

context.unit: individual working or streaming while travelling
context.geography: any destination with unlimited or high-volume plans offered

triggers.text: Need to work or navigate continuously without monitoring usage
Discovery that an unlimited plan throttles after a daily fair-use threshold

constraints.text: Unlimited regional plans reported capped near 1 Mbps after roughly 3 GB/day
Heavy tethering described as impractical under those thresholds

disqualifiers.text: Light user for whom a small fixed-GB plan is cheaper

open_questions: Fair-use thresholds are plan- and date-specific; the single independent figure retrieved needs re-verification per package before any factual claim is made.

icps.label: Traveller blocked or uncertain at the device and identity layer: eSIM support, carrier lock, device origin, or destination ID registration

context.blocking_layer: handset capability, carrier lock, or local line-registration rules

triggers.text: Most-viewed help questions are device compatibility and installation
Carrier-locked handsets described as the most common complaint from new users
Uncertainty about whether a digital line escapes local identity-registration rules

roles.label: traveller checking device eligibility before buying
home carrier that must release the device lock

constraints.text: Device must be eSIM-capable and unlocked
Some handsets sold in China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan lack compatibility
A digital line may still fall under local SIM-registration law

disqualifiers.text: Handset with no eSIM support and no willingness to change device

open_questions: Which destinations actually enforce identity registration on travel eSIMs? The retrieved source names none and is undated.

icps.label: Post-purchase traveller already in destination: no service after landing, package expiry, or top-up decisions

context.state: line purchased and installed, or purchased and failing

triggers.text: 'Why is my eSIM not working?' listed among the most-viewed help questions
'When does my eSIM data package expire?' listed among the most-viewed help questions
Top-up described as an alternative to buying a new line

constraints.text: A failing digital line cannot be moved to another handset
Support response times reported as slow by community sources

open_questions: Failure modes are known only through help-article titles and one independent review; no first-party ticket-mix evidence is available.

icps.label: Business, affiliate or reseller partner distributing travel connectivity to end customers

context.unit: organisation reselling or bundling travel connectivity

triggers.text: A partner/reseller programme and an affiliate category are published by the target

open_questions: No independent or behavioural evidence of partner-side demand, roles, criteria or language was found. This ICP is excluded from the panel until such evidence exists or a human promotes it.
